A. WALLACE FORGIE AND THE ORIGIN OF C.S.E.T.
Two books, read in full text rather than in snippets, found 2026-09-07 by a
QUOTED "Wallace Forgie" sweep of the Internet Archive book corpus.

=====================================================================
1. THE C.S.E.T. MANUAL FOR TUXIS BOYS (1918) -- THE PRIMARY SOURCE
   archive.org item cihm_66450. [Toronto]: C.S.E.T. of the National Council
   of Young Men's Christian Associations of Canada, 1918. Fully downloadable.
=====================================================================

From the acknowledgements, immediately after a list of the committee's
denominational members:

  "a mention should be made of the work of Capt. A. Wallace Forgie, Secretary
  of the C.S.E.T. Committee, who has been indefatigable in the correlation of
  the mass of information and material considered by the Committee. On his
  going to France in September last the work was continued by Mr. Gordon K.
  [H]ignell a well-known boys' worker of the Central West.

  We announce with the deepest regret that just as the press work of this book
  was completed, M[r]. Hignell contracted pneumonia and passed away in
  Winnipeg, on October 21, 1918, just one week after he had returned from
  Toronto and his labors in connection with this book. Mr. Hignell had served
  overseas and on his return again took up Boys' Work."

TWO THINGS THIS SETTLES OUTRIGHT:
  * THE NAME FORM. "Capt. A. Wallace Forgie", printed by his own committee in
    1918. This project had reasoned its way to "A. Wallace" from an obituary
    and a roster and said so; here it is, stated.
  * THE OFFICE. He was SECRETARY OF THE C.S.E.T. COMMITTEE -- the body that
    produced the programme -- and the manual credits him with correlating its
    material. He went to France in September 1918.

=====================================================================
2. THE BOY'S OWN BOOK (1929) -- THE PROGRAMME'S OWN ORIGIN STORY
   archive.org item boysownbook00shei. Toronto: National Boys' Work Board of
   the Religious Education Council of Canada, copyright 1929. Fully
   downloadable. This is the governing body of the programme telling its own
   history seventeen years after the fact.
=====================================================================

  "* * in 1912, just seventeen years ago, that the forerunner of our present
  Trail Ranger and Tuxis programmes was prepared and published. The group of
  men who laid the foundation of our present programmes was appointed by the
  National Council of the Young Men's Christian Association. The moving spirit
  in and through it all was Mr. Taylor Statten, then secretary of the Boys'
  Work Committee of the National Council Y.M.C.A.

  The origin, however, goes back another five years, during which period
  Messrs. Taylor Statten and Wallace Forgie, as Boys' Work Secretaries of the
  Central Branch of the Y.M.C.A., in Toronto, were carrying on experiments
  which in 1912 were to blossom out into what were then called the Canadian
  Standard Efficiency Tests. IT WAS IN 1907 THAT MR. FORGIE GOT THE IDEA OF
  LUKE 2:52, 'And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature and in favour with God
  and man,' AS A BASIS FOR SUCH A PROGRAMME. It was about this time also that
  the idea of charting boys on a four-fold scale was first practiced.

  Simple as were these first attempts to formulate a four-fold programme based
  on Luke 2:52, they met with an instant response from both Sunday School and
  Association [boys] ..."

And later, on the revision:

  "... that further improvement could be made. The little red handbook had
  rendered yeoman service. FORTY-TWO THOUSAND HAD BEEN USED but we were ready
  for something better. The programme, it was felt, should be clothed in more
  attractive form. There should be insignia, initiation ceremonies, badge work
  projects and possibly a division of the programme with more appealing
  activities for boys from twelve to fourteen.

  MR. FORGIE OF THE Y.M.C.A. WAS ASKED TO DIRECT THE WORK of incorporating
  these new ideas in a revised programme. The assistance of a large body of
  experienced men was secured. Magistrate J. Edmund Jones, particularly, made
  a splendid contribution.

  When Mr. Forgie returned to the front, Gordon Hignell, of Winnipeg, was set
  aside by the Association to complete the work of publication. This was his
  last task ...

  Finally in October 1918, the work was complete. THE NAME 'CANADIAN STANDARD
  EFFICIENCY TRAINING' BECAME A [...]"

=====================================================================
WHAT THE TWO SOURCES DO TOGETHER
=====================================================================

They were published eleven years apart, by two different bodies -- the YMCA's
National Council and the Religious Education Council of Canada -- and they
agree in detail: Forgie directing the revision, Forgie leaving for the front,
Hignell of Winnipeg finishing it, the work complete in October 1918. The 1918
manual adds Hignell's death on 21 October 1918, a week after he came back from
Toronto; the 1929 book adds the forty-two thousand copies of the little red
handbook and the reason for the revision.

AND THEY GIVE C.S.E.T. A CHRONOLOGY THIS PROJECT DOES NOT HAVE:

  1907   Forgie, at Toronto Central with Statten, takes Luke 2:52 as the basis
         of a fourfold programme; charting boys on a four-fold scale begins
  1912   the forerunner is prepared and published as the CANADIAN STANDARD
         EFFICIENCY TESTS -- the "little red handbook", 42,000 used
  ----   Forgie directs the revision: insignia, initiation ceremonies, badge
         work, and a division for boys of twelve to fourteen
  Sept
  1918   Forgie goes to France; Hignell takes over
  Oct
  1918   the work is complete and the name becomes CANADIAN STANDARD
         EFFICIENCY TRAINING

NOTE THE TWO EXPANSIONS OF ONE ACRONYM. 1912 gives Canadian Standard
Efficiency TESTS; October 1918 gives Canadian Standard Efficiency TRAINING.
They are not the same programme under one name; they are two programmes, the
second a deliberate revision of the first, and the acronym survived the change.

=====================================================================
THE CONFLICT THIS RAISES, WHICH IS NOT RESOLVED HERE
=====================================================================

This project's articles say "In 1914, he [Statten] established the Canadian
Standards Efficiency Training (CSET) program", and a V1 verify pass in
February 2026 recorded "CSET 1914" as independently confirmed. NEITHER OF
THESE TWO SOURCES SUPPORTS 1914. One gives 1912 for the Tests and October 1918
for the Training, and the other, printed in 1918 by the programme's own
committee, is silent on the founding date but consistent with it.

1914 may be right about something these two do not describe. It is not
overwritten here. A conflict record is raised instead.

AND THE ATTRIBUTION QUESTION IS SEPARATE FROM THE DATE. Both articles credit
CSET to Taylor Statten alone. The 1929 book, published by the programme's own
board, calls Statten "the moving spirit in and through it all" AND gives the
originating idea to Forgie in 1907 and the direction of the 1918 revision to
Forgie as well. That is not a contradiction of Statten's role; it is a second
name that this project's account leaves out entirely.

=====================================================================
3. INTERNATIONAL COUNCIL OF RELIGIOUS EDUCATION YEARBOOK 1924
   archive.org item yearbook0000inte_m3q0. Fully downloadable.
=====================================================================

  "Boys' Secretary, A. W. Forgie, 302 I. O. O. F. Building, Calgary, Alberta"
  (printed twice)
  "A. Wallace Forgie, Boys' Work Secretary, Alberta Religious Education
  Council"

So the Alberta post is dated to 1924 and given an address, and it is the
ALBERTA RELIGIOUS EDUCATION COUNCIL rather than the YMCA -- which is the same
kind of body that published The Boy's Own Book, and is worth noticing: after
CSET, Forgie's employer was the religious-education side of the movement, not
the association side.

=====================================================================
LEADS NOT FOLLOWED, FROM THE SAME SWEEP -- ALL SNIPPETS, NONE READ
=====================================================================

  algonquinstory0000saun -- Audrey Saunders, "Algonquin Story": a camp of the
    Taylor Statten Camps "directed by Wallace Forgie". Three scans of it.
  nastawgancanadia0000unse -- "Nastawgan": a Temagami canoe trip "with his
    assistant Wallace Forgie".
  worldservice0000lato -- "Dunderdale was sent from Canada to replace Wallace
    Forgie for work for boys in South India".
  canadabritishwor0000unse -- "Maj. Wallace Forgie, Comrades to Canadian Boys
    and the Four Square" (note the RANK: Capt. in 1918, Maj. here).
  asianexperiment0000elma -- a weekend at Camp Tonakela with its founder.
  richbrothmemoirs0000reec -- a Canadian diplomat's memoir: "on the upper
    slopes of middle age, Wallace Forgie. He lived in spartan conditions..."
  mydesire0000wats -- "met such men as E. A. Corbett and Wallace Forgie".
  everettboydjacks00pier -- a life shaped "chiefly through the inspiration of
    Mr. Wallace Forgie, who became his ideal and his intimate [friend]".
